newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tietmeyer generally satisfied with exchange rates.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer generally satisfied with exchange rates.

text.p: German Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday he was generally satisfied with current exchange rates and hopes the single European currency will be stable and competitive against the dollar and the yen.
"As regards the current exchange rate situation in Europe and overseas, we are generally satisfied," Tietmeyer said in an interview to be broadcast on French television TF1.
He had been asked by an interviewer to comment on what he thought the value of the euro should be relative to the dollar.
"I hope, first of all, that the euro will be a stable currency that will be competitive with the two other currencies," he said, referring to the dollar and the yen.

"As for the precise setting of the rate, that is not possible at this time. It will depend on the fundamental conditions in Europe, on the one hand, and in America, on the other, and on their development," he said.
A transcript of the interview in French was provided by TF1 and translated into English by Reuters.
